items.title: In Odesa, no-one is safe from Russia's new Black Sea strikes
items.description: Blackened ships and smashed docks mark Russia's recent surge of attacks on Ukraine's coastline.

items.title: Iran says deal with Oman on Strait of Hormuz is in final stages
items.description: Neither the US or Oman have commented on the proposed agreement on the vital waterway.

items.title: Indian journalist Tarun Tejpal sentenced to 10 years in jail for rape
items.description: Tejpal, who has denied the accusations, can appeal against the verdict in India's Supreme Court.

items.title: Iranian footballers who defied Tehran become Australian citizens
items.description: There were among seven to be granted humanitarian visas while playing in Australia - but the other five changed their minds and returned to Iran.

items.title: Rihanna is 'in the studio', says partner A$AP Rocky
items.description: The singer, who last released a full album in 2016, is in the studio and "cooking", her partner said.

items.title: Outrage as Ugandan football captain beaten to death in street gang attack
items.description: The 27-year-old was killed by suspected robbers after resisting an attempt to rob him, police say.

items.title: Air India's new CEO faces financial and safety turbulence
items.description: The aftermath of last's year deadly crash and mounting financial losses will be Gebremariam's main challenges.

items.title: Afghan boxer accused of killing Scottish aid worker back in court
items.description: Sharif Ahmadzai, who is 26 and from Afghanistan, faces charges of homicide with intent, robbery and weapons offences.

items.title: Nigerian security forces rescue more than 300 abductees
items.description: The government says the rescue is the country's largest single-day operation by joint security forces.

items.title: After deadly Kyiv strike, Ukraine warns interceptor shortage is costing lives
items.description: Without Patriot interceptors, Ukraine's skies are wide open and people are fully exposed to Russia's missile barrages.

items.title: Meta becomes latest firm to say its AI hacked another company
items.description: Meta is the latest company to disclose an AI agent breach, raising cyber-security concerns.

items.title: Drone carrying explosives found at German airport, police say
items.description: The drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes before another object collided with a cargo aircraft in mid-air.

items.title: Israel strikes south Lebanon after two soldiers killed by explosion
items.description: Lebanese authorities says one person was killed in the strikes, which came after the first Israeli military fatalities in Lebanon in more than a month.

items.title: Ex-leader Hasina gambles on return to Bangladesh despite death penalty
items.description: The 78-year-old has been convicted of crimes against humanity over a deadly crackdown on a 2024 uprising.

items.title: Youth protests have weakened Modi, Indian activist who went on hunger strike tells BBC
items.description: The "cockroach" movement was one of the biggest public displays of dissent against India's prime minister in years.

items.title: UN rights chief alarmed by rise in Iran executions since March
items.description: Volker Türk says 56 people have been executed on national security-related charges, including 27 in cases linked to January's protests.

items.title: Why some scientists are thrilled that a SpaceX rocket has crashed into the Moon
items.description: While the collision was an accident, it is a unique scientific gift for planetary geologists that could provide important data for future space missions.

items.title: Waste workers help winner find binned €1m lottery ticket in Italy
items.description: The player only realised they binned the life-changing ticket after family told them the numbers he played for years had been drawn.

items.title: South Africa plans new rules on ex-leaders' foreign trips after Zuma's visit to India
items.description: Jacob Zuma was pictured with a businessmen allegedly at the heart of a corruption scandal in South Africa

items.title: Banned from football at home, Afghan women's team reunite 8,000 miles away
items.description: Women in the team, which is recognised by Fifa, say football has given them freedom and independence.
